reason: Upstream hosts a Chrome DevTools debugging target in a worker thread: console evaluation and breakpoints in the host, the cordis tree as the Elements panel and unredacted fetch capture as the Network panel. A Go process has no JavaScript engine to attach to and the DevTools frontend is already dropped, so the target, code evaluation and client inspection are not built (DH-ADR-XINSPECT-1). The two harness-specific views become owner-only host pages with command-line twins (the runtime tree and a masked ring of recent HTTP exchanges), and CPU, memory and scheduler inspection comes from Go runtime profiles behind a second switch.

The package is only a profile patch that switches on the inspector with fetch capture, the session inspector and the statistics view. In Go it is the devtools optional bundle, one disabled group of the x.inspect and x.stats entries in area A27's optional list, with profiling as a separately disabled entry inside it; no package of its own remains.

Upstream is a React sidebar page that tabulates the session records and the chat engine's node objects already loaded in the browser. The Go host renders a session log page from A06's Query: every event paged over the whole log, grouped by turn and step, filtered by type and surface class, with event detail and a panel of fold states at the cut. The chat-node presentation, object-reference navigation and the click-to-pick mask are not built because the Go UI has no client object graph; a row links to the transcript and trajectory by seq instead.

Upstream folds the browser's loaded event window into turn and step rows with six client-side definitions. Go registers one row projection, stepStats, in A06's projection registry, so the figures cover the whole log and survive paging, and renders the Statistics page on the host from those rows with totals from A06's stats view and A04's tokenUsage. The same fold is offered to the trajectory view so that both show the same per-step numbers.

Timeline is kept as a compiled-in, default-off component under internal/x/timeline: five model tools, ten typed durable event types holding whole values, a projection for trees and discussions, replacement of todo_write through A03's Restrict and deny-only guard, owner edits, tree export and import, and timed reports as report rows. Changed: each report call is requested by a flushed event and settled by exactly one attempt event, there is no repair call, reports are paged by day with no seven-day window, and the UI is host-rendered regions instead of a React sidebar.

The bundle exists to give the query tools a private in-memory SQLite index, because upstream's shipped bundles turn search off. In Go the search index is rows in the session store written with each event and is on by default (DH-D-VIEW-6), so nothing of the bundle remains except the switch: the session-recall optional bundle that mounts the x.recall tools.

The five read-only history tools are kept with their names as a default-off component, x.recall, that translates arguments into A06's Query calls with the calling agent's visibility. The package's own authorisation by cwd string, its failure sanitiser and its exclusive scheduling are not carried over: visibility, bounds, stable cursors and error codes are properties of Query. The fixed guidance section is kept.

The importer of DeepSeek chat website exports is kept as a default-off P2 component, x.chatimport, separate from the deferred upstream-session import of DH-ADR-11. Kept: newest conversations first, one branch per conversation, original times, pinned titles, cold writes without an agent, per-conversation isolation. Changed: the archive is a staged file or a directory read with archive/zip instead of an in-memory buffer, a command-line entry exists beside the upload form, each session is published only after it is complete, re-import is detected, and searches are imported as text and not as fabricated tool calls.

The statistics view is still not part of the default product: it is mounted only by the devtools optional bundle. What is removed is the installation step, because the view is compiled into the one binary and one switch enables it.
justification: Kept on purpose: design.md section 4.2 makes every experimental capability a default-off entry under internal/x, and area A27 lists each as a disabled optional bundle. Promotion to the default product is a later owner decision, not a design gap. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: Start times are lost upstream because the fold runs over the browser's loaded window. The stepStats row projection folds the whole log on the host, so every step row holds its start and the page never shows 'start unknown'; DH-T-XINSPECT-7 asserts it.

Upstream's inner calls carry no turn or step, so the view merges them by root-call context. In Go a nested call made through the tool command line is logged inside the bracket of its outer tool call with session, turn and step attribution (design.md section 4.4), so the fold attributes it to the step of the outer call by position and needs no separate context or merge.

The limit describes contention for the one in-flight history page that Chat, Trajectory and Statistics share inside upstream's React client. The Go UI has no client-side session window: each page request is its own bounded host read (DH-ADR-3), so there is nothing to retry.

Upstream has no whole-session wall clock and substitutes model time plus summed tool time. The stepStats rows hold each step's start and end and tool time both as a sum and as the union of intervals, so the totals row shows active wall time as the sum of turn intervals and parallel tools are not double counted.

Upstream exempted this view from a recorded-session scenario. The Go design requires one from the start: DH-T-XINSPECT-7 replays a recorded session keylessly through the built binary and compares the statistics table with a golden file.

A ghost turn arises upstream when compaction restates a result for a turn that has left the loaded window. The Go fold sees every turn's start in the whole log and files each event under the turn and step it belongs to, so a restated result cannot open a row of its own.

Timing is still derived from committed events and not sampled: total time is last step end minus first step start, and queue or scheduler waits land in a 'rest' segment. Improved: first-token and model time are plain fields the LLM runtime records on each attempt event, and tool time is kept both as a sum and as a union.
justification: Kept on purpose: a view may read committed session events only (design.md section 4.6), so there is no second sampler whose figures could disagree with the log. DH-D-XINSPECT-3 builds the fold with the recorded attempt timings. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: The limit is about who owns and revokes browser object URLs for prompt images in a shared React image cache, and about hover previews on touch clients. The Go host serves an attachment through area A19's session.attachment route as an ordinary image address, so no object URL exists to own (DH-ADR-3).

Upstream keeps the whole upload, up to 512 MiB, in host memory. The Go importer streams the upload to an owner-only staging file in the harness home (or reads a path given on the command line) and opens it with archive/zip, which reads one entry at a time through random access, so memory is bounded by one conversation and one image.

fflate pushes inflated bytes, so a small declared size with highly compressed data keeps the host busy until the entry ends. Go's reader is pulled by the caller: each entry is read through a reader that fails as soon as it passes MaxEntryBytes or its declared size and checks cancellation between reads, so the limit stops the work and not only the retention (DH-LIB-FFLATE-R2).

Upstream's streaming pass walks local file headers, so a second local header with an existing name can deliver an extra conversation. archive/zip returns entries from the central directory only, duplicate names there are refused, and each selected conversation id is written at most once, so data that the directory does not list is never read.

Upstream's failure response for an archive that breaks mid-way does not list the sessions already written. A Go import is a host-tracked operation whose final result always lists the sessions it published, also when it ends in failure or cancellation; DH-T-XINSPECT-13 and -14 assert it.

Upstream has two read paths, one of which truncates an over-long entry and re-parses the directory on every call. The Go importer has one read path: the directory is parsed once when the archive is opened, and an entry longer than it declares is an error, never a truncated value (DH-LIB-FFLATE-R2).

The carrier path without byte progress exists for pages whose host runs in another JavaScript execution context, the browser-worker preview. That runtime is dropped (DH-ADR-17), and the one Go upload path is an ordinary HTTP form post whose progress the browser knows.
The Go importer also targets one structure of export format version 3, reads later-added fields as optional, refuses another version and skips record types it does not know.
justification: Kept on purpose: the format belongs to the vendor's website, is not specified for third parties and can change without notice, so supporting generations nobody can test would be a claim without evidence. DH-D-XINSPECT-7 builds the version check and the per-conversation skip with a coded reason. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: Upstream accepts only a browser upload of a ZIP. The Go importer takes an fs.FS, so the command dsh session import-chat accepts a ZIP path or an extracted export directory on the host machine, and the web form remains for remote hosts.

Upstream does not record what it imported, so a second import duplicates every session. The Go importer writes the conversation id and its update time into the store's imported_from column and skips a conversation already present unless the caller asks for a copy; the result counts what was skipped.

A file whose bytes the export does not contain still cannot be opened after import. Changed: it becomes a text note with its name and size in the user message, not a file handle that names a path holding nothing, so the model is not sent to read an empty path.
justification: Kept on purpose: the bytes of non-image files and of some images are not in the vendor's export, so no importer can restore them. DH-D-XINSPECT-7 builds the note form. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: Upstream stores every image before parsing any conversation and has no removal, so images of failed or dropped conversations stay forever. The Go importer stores a conversation's images just before its events, and area A07's retention collects any blob that no event references after its grace period (DH-D-STORAGE-9).

Upstream cannot remove a session whose workspace attachment failed. In Go each conversation is prepared invisibly, attached to the workspace and only then published; if the attachment fails the prepared session is discarded, so no session exists outside the workspace.

Upstream needs its own maxTitleBytes because the title service hides its limit. The Go importer has no such field: it normalises and pins the title through area A06's title service, whose configured limit applies.

The Go importer leaves out the same content: other branches, content-filtered rounds, risk disclaimers, tips, page finds, partial-read notices, encrypted link bodies, the pinned flag, per-token times and accumulated token usage.
justification: Kept on purpose: a session is a linear log so one branch is chosen, and the other records are either never shown as reply text by the vendor's site or must not enter the model's context. Search result links are imported as text. DH-D-XINSPECT-7 builds the mapping. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: Upstream writes fixed English explanations into the log and shows the host's English message in the dialog. The Go importer records a code and its data for an excluded reply and for every failure reason, and the page text comes from the message catalogue in the reader's language (English and Chinese complete).

Upstream imports searches and opened pages as web_search and web_fetch calls that have no request-header tool record and an inferred status code. The Go importer writes them as Markdown text inside the assistant message, so no tool call that this harness never made exists in history and nothing is inferred.

Upstream's inspection views need the web application. In Go the pages are served by the host to any browser, and the tree, the HTTP capture and profiling also have dsh debug commands, while the session log is reachable through dsh session show and export, so a headless host can be inspected too.

Upstream warns that enabling the bundle starts unredacted capture and a local code-execution endpoint, with no dedicated control. In Go there is no code-execution endpoint, capture masks credentials and keeps no body by default, and the bundle and the separate profiling entry are ordinary switches in the settings forms.

Upstream's Memory and Performance panels cover only the host's V8 heap and CPU. In Go the host is measured with runtime profiles and execution traces (DH-D-XINSPECT-2), and the page in the browser is an ordinary document that the browser's own developer tools profile, because no client runtime is hidden behind a synthetic context.

The limit describes a WebSocket relay that stops when the host's JavaScript main thread is paused by the V8 debugger. A Go host has no JavaScript thread and no debugger relay; the debugging target is not built (DH-ADR-XINSPECT-1).

The limit is about breakpoints in upstream's browser client runtime reached through a synthetic CDP context. The Go UI has no client plugin runtime (DH-ADR-3) and no CDP target (DH-ADR-XINSPECT-1); the page's small scripts are debugged with the browser's own tools.

The limit is about which JavaScript bundles the client side of the inspector catalogs for the DevTools Sources panel. There is no Sources panel and no client bundle to catalog (DH-ADR-XINSPECT-1, DH-ADR-3).

The limit is about evaluating JavaScript typed into the DevTools console inside the page, which a content security policy can block. The Go design has no evaluation at all (DH-ADR-XINSPECT-1), and the page's strict content security policy stays as it is.

The limit is about giving each browser tab a stable identity as a CDP source through the Web Locks API. No tab is an inspection source in Go (DH-ADR-XINSPECT-1); a tab's identity for the event stream is area A19's tab id.

Upstream replaces globalThis.fetch, so direct Undici calls and fetch references taken earlier escape capture. In Go capture is one transport wrapper registered with egress, the single factory of outbound HTTP clients, so every client is observed whenever it was built; DH-T-XINSPECT-2 asserts it. What is still not seen, child-process traffic and WebSocket frames, is stated in the specification.

Upstream tees both bodies by default and its retained-body limit does not cover buffering inside the tee. In Go bodies are not kept unless Bodies is set; then a prefix of at most MaxBodyBytes is copied into a fixed buffer as the caller reads, so there is no queue that a slow reader can grow, and the ring is also bounded by total bytes.

The limit is about restarting the worker thread that holds CDP state. The Go design has no worker and no CDP state (DH-ADR-XINSPECT-1); a diagnostic component is an ordinary fiber that the loader reloads like any other.

Upstream's tables see only the history window loaded in the browser. The Go log page asks the host for bounded pages by seq over the whole log, can jump to any seq, and applies its filters in the query, so no record is out of reach and row identity is the seq.

Upstream's log view does not show projection updates. The Go page has a 'views at this cut' panel that lists every registered fold with its state (current, behind, pending or failed) and the seq it covers, read from A06's registry Snapshot and Status.

Upstream highlights rows only when the client store publishes, and warns that raw data is unredacted. In Go a new row arrives as one fragment per committed event from the session stream, so there is no publication cadence; the page is owner-only, and secret values are never written to the session log in the first place (design.md section 6).

Upstream copies a row-reference array per publication and scans all loaded rows to filter and lay out. The Go host renders one bounded page per request (LogPageSize) with the filter applied by the query, and DH-T-XINSPECT-5 asserts that rows read per page do not grow with the log.

The limit is the keyboard selection state of a React suggestion list that refreshes asynchronously. The Go page has no client-side list state: its type and class filters are ordinary form fields that the host applies on each request (DH-ADR-3), so there is no list whose selection could be lost.

Upstream locates a record only if the chat is already displayed and the node rendered, because it searches the chat's DOM. A Go log row is a link to the transcript or trajectory address of its seq; following it opens that view and loads the history page that holds the target. The click-to-pick mask in the other direction is not built (DH-ADR-XINSPECT-4).

The bundle's in-memory index is rebuilt after every restart. In Go there is no second index: search documents are rows written in the transaction of their event in the session store, available at once in every process and after a restart (DH-D-VIEW-6). Search stays limited to what the caller's visibility admits.

Upstream's projection holds reports in memory and the view shows seven days of them. In Go reports are derived rows (timeline_report) that the reports view pages a day at a time, so any period can be opened and nothing scans a retained list. The number of open discussions stays bounded by the MaxDiscussions setting, default 512.
A task update still writes the whole current tree as one session event. The cap is the session's event size limit together with MaxTasks, in place of upstream's separate 2 MiB figure.
justification: Kept on purpose: design.md section 4.6 requires a state-carrying session event to hold the whole new value and never a delta, so that the latest event alone restores the state and replay is last-write-wins. DH-D-XINSPECT-4 builds the bounded tree event. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: Pause and continue are still requests that reach the agent as an inbox notice and take effect when the model updates the plan; stopping an active turn is the driver's cancel.
justification: Kept on purpose: a pause changes a plan, which the agent that owns the plan must record, while cancellation is a different act with a recorded cause owned by the agent loop (DH-O-3). Merging them would let a panel click abort tool calls mid-flight. The panel labels the control as a request and shows Stop beside it; DH-D-XINSPECT-4 builds it. The stage is a placeholder because the implementation plan is not written.

reason: Upstream withholds a continuation token because its cursors go stale when the corpus changes. A06's keyset cursors are properties of single documents and stay valid, so both search tools take a cursor argument and return next_cursor; a capped page no longer forces the model to guess a narrower query.

Upstream compares cwd strings, so two paths to one directory do not share authority. The Go tools use A06's visibility, which rests on workspace membership recorded against the workspace's canonical path (area A07), so a symbolic link to the workspace is the same workspace; DH-T-XINSPECT-11 asserts it.

Upstream returns complete payloads inline unless a deployment also mounts the spill policy. In Go a result bound is part of the one tool pipeline for every tool (DH-O-6), and the tools ask Query for bounded windows and snippets, so no composition can return an unbounded event.

The Go harness exposes session_search when the session-recall bundle is on, changed: it calls Query.Search grouped by session with the agent's visibility, never returns the caller's own session, and adds a mode argument (ranked or literal) and a cursor with next_cursor; the availability filter is dropped because one store has no live-or-stored source. Every other upstream argument is kept under its upstream name: query, session_ids, created_at_from, created_at_to, parent_session_ids, include_root_sessions, event_seq_from, event_seq_to, event_time_from, event_time_to, event_types and event_surfaces.

The Go harness exposes session_event_search when the session-recall bundle is on, changed: it calls Query.Search inside one visible session, ends before the step that made the call when the target is the current session, and adds mode and cursor arguments.

The Go harness exposes session_trace unchanged in purpose: it calls Query.Lineage and returns the ancestors and descendants the caller may see, bounded by LineageMaxNodes, with a marker that carries no id where a boundary is hidden.

The Go harness exposes session_event_trace unchanged in purpose: it calls Query.Trace and returns what replaced one event and what cites it, read from A06's derived class and link rows without replaying the log.

The Go harness exposes session_event_read, changed: it calls Query.Event and returns the hot part of one event with at most ReadWindowMax neighbour summaries per side, and the pipeline's result bound applies last, where upstream returned the unabridged event inline.

Upstream emits this event from the Timeline storage service to the Timeline reminder module of the same package when a user edit moves a task into or out of the top priority. In Go producer and consumer are one package, so no typed event is declared: the edit handler calls the notice function directly, and the notice reaches the model through the agent's inbox. The durable record of the edit is the timeline/priority session event.
chatimport.Config replaces it: MaxSessions 1,000, MaxArchiveBytes 512 MiB and MaxEntryBytes 256 MiB. maxTitleBytes has no counterpart because the title service's own limit applies.

Six of the 24 fields map onto inspect.Config (MaxExchanges, Bodies, MaxBodyBytes, MaxTotalBytes, MaxTreeNodes, plus LogPageSize which is new); the other 18 size the worker thread, the CDP bridge, client sources and reconnects, none of which exists. profile.Config (MaxSeconds, Kinds) is new and belongs to a separately disabled entry.

timeline.Config replaces it with the same defaults: ReplaceTodo true (upstream allowTodo false), ReminderSteps 24, MaxTasks 500, MaxTrees 30, Reports false (upstream true; a recommended default, not confirmed by the owner, so that reports need their own switch), Interval 15 minutes, RollupFactors 4 and 4, MaxConcurrent 2, Timeout 120 seconds, MaxResponseBytes 65,536, ReportMaxTokens 4,096, the language and the three guidance texts; MaxDiscussions 512 becomes a field. The three display settings become per-viewer preferences, and the rule that report periods increase and stay within seven days is a validator on the struct.
recall.Config replaces it: MaxSearchResults 100, capped by A06's MaxLimit, and SearchTimeout 30 seconds, which becomes the tool deadline of the two search tools.

ctx.deepseekChatImport becomes the service key chatimport.Key with the interface Importer (Limits, Plan, Run). The upload route and the command are carriers that call it; the owner-only rule is the route's access rule and the command's admin class.

The note decides that the inspector reads data the browser already holds, adds no stream or storage, navigates object graphs through weak references and finds chat elements through the DOM, and that a default-off bundle also starts the debugging worker with unredacted capture. In Go the host owns the data: it pages the whole log through Query, so there is no loaded window, no object graph and no DOM contract; the chat-node view and the picker are dropped and a row links by seq. The default-off bundle is kept as the devtools optional bundle, without a debugging worker and with masked capture.

Kept from the note: selection of the newest conversations from the export's index, the branch that ends at current_message_id, one turn per user message, original non-decreasing times, a pinned title, cold writes without a live agent, per-conversation isolation and one import at a time. Changed: the note rejects staging on disk and a host path, and Go adopts both (a staged file read with archive/zip, and a command that takes a path or directory); a session is published only when complete; re-import is detected through imported_from; searches and opened pages are text, not fabricated tool calls; reasons are codes. It is a separate importer from the deferred upstream-session import of DH-ADR-11.

title: No debugging target: the DevTools hub, code evaluation and client inspection are not built
Diagnostics are read-only, owner-only, bounded, masked by default and never sent
Profiles are exposed to the owner on a local host, behind a second switch
The raw log and the statistics are host pages over Query and one fold; the chat-node view and the element picker are dropped
Timeline is a compiled-in, default-off component whose report calls are logged auxiliary calls
The history tools are a thin, default-off consumer of Query; there is no second index
Chat import is its own importer, separate from the upstream-session import, sharing only the write path
A developer sees the live component tree and recent outbound HTTP on an owner-only page
The owner of a local host can take a CPU, memory or scheduler profile from it
Any session can be read event by event, and its time and tokens are broken down per turn and step
The agent keeps a weighted task tree that a person can follow, discuss and steer
Timed reports summarise the work at several intervals, and every report call is in the log
The model can search and read earlier sessions of its workspace
Conversations exported from the vendor's chat website become sessions that can be continued
The runtime tree snapshot is complete, bounded and read-only
HTTP capture sees every egress client, masks credentials, keeps no body by default and stays bounded
Every route of the area is owner-only, absent with its bundle off, and no CDP, evaluation or sending path exists
Profiling is off by default, refused in remote mode, single, clamped and cancellable, and net/http/pprof is never imported
The session log page groups, filters and pages a recorded session with bounded reads
The stepStats fold equals a refold and matches golden logs and the session totals
Keyless replay of a recorded session yields the golden statistics table with every start time
Timeline progress, limits, fork behaviour and tree export and import
In a composed host Timeline replaces todo_write, withholds planning tools from subagents, reminds, notifies and unloads cleanly
A report request is logged before it is sent and settled by exactly one attempt, within the concurrency and schedule rules
The five history tools respect visibility, exclusions, cursors and result bounds through the executor
The chat conversation converter maps golden conversations to the expected event drafts
Import orchestration: limits stop work, refusals write nothing, failures leave no partial session, re-import is skipped, staging is removed
The import upload route is owner-only, bounded and always ends with a result that lists written sessions
In a real browser: tree, masked HTTP capture, a profile, the log and the statistics of a real session
A real model plans with the task tree, survives a host kill, and a timed report is logged before it is sent
A real model finds earlier work in its own workspace and nothing outside it
A real export from the vendor's chat website is imported twice and one conversation is continued
